title: release_versions reads as a release a tag its template cannot make, where release.tag holds {version} twice
body:
## What happened

Found while 0352-1 made release_tag_version (lib/helpers) the reading of a tag back to its version, for release target and formula's tag_version. release_versions (lib/release.steps), which every bump and release_previous_tag read, matches a tag by the text before and after the template's first `{version}`, and takes what lies between as the version when it is an X.Y.Z. It never fills the template back, as release_tag_version does. So where release.tag holds `{version}` more than once, eg `v{version}-{version}`, a tag holding the text `{version}` itself, eg `v1.2.3-{version}`, reads as release 1.2.3, though no cut could make that tag. release_tag_version refuses it.

Neither reading can read such a template's real tags: the cut makes `v1.2.3-1.2.3`, which neither matches, so `--patch` finds no newest release. release.tag's value rule only asks that `{version}` appear, so it takes such a template.

## Why it matters

Two readings of one question give two answers, and release_versions is the one every bump reads. Low, since it takes a template with `{version}` twice and a tag holding braces pushed by hand.

## Options, none chosen

- release_versions reads each tag through release_tag_version, so the two cannot disagree.
- release.tag's value rule takes `{version}` once only, so no template has a second one to disagree over.

0352-1 left release_versions as it is, on vc's word that a reading that differs keeps its behaviour and is filed.

## Resolution

cc, 2026-11-17 13:07Z by date -u: fixed by unit 0371-1, landed at 8234f074 for 0.1.27, from the bank tested at 0d26574b on 0355-1's landing. Both options, on vc's GO. release.tag's value rule (lib/config) takes {version} once: a template holding it twice is refused, naming the key, since a tag made from it is read back to no version and no bump could find the release it names. release_versions (lib/release.steps), which every bump and release_previous_tag read, reads each tag through release_tag_version (lib/helpers), the one reading of a tag back to its version, which formula's tag_version and release target read through too; its loop keeps issue 0106's if. The rule refuses nothing in use: of the 26 estate configs under prj, cfg and writing, Utilz alone declares release.tag, as "{version}" (vc's measure). configuration.md's release.tag row says {version} once.

Arms in releasecore.bats: release.tag v{version}-{version} refused at validation, naming the key and why; and release_versions under a two-{version} template reading a brace tag, and a cut's fill, as no release, with a single-{version} control reading the one release tag. Both were red at the base and green at the tip under BSD and GNU, with releasecore.bats and formula.bats whole, releasecut's 17 arms that bump, resolve or resume a version or read the previous release's tag, and releaselegs' two 0333 arms green, test scans 61 of 61 and check lint 0 breaches over 59 files (Desk slot 01M7MRTVQT5W15K8GM4KSXCN6N).
